original_value: Achieving the shift towards Industry 4.0 is only feasible through the active integration of the shopfloor into the transformation process. Several shopfloor management (SM) systems can aid this conversion. They form two major factions. The first includes methodologies such as Balanced Scorecard (BSC). A defining feature is rigid structures to fixate on pre-defined goals. Other SM strategies instead concentrate on continuous improvement by giving directions. An example of this group is the “HOSHIN KANRI TREE” (HKT). One way of analyzing the dissimilarities, the advantages and disadvantages of these groups, is to examine the neurological patterns of workers as they are applying these. This paper aims to achieve this evaluation through non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) sensors, which capture the electrical activity of the brain. A deep learning (DL) soft sensor is used to classify the recorded data with an accuracy of 96.5%. Through this result and an analysis using the correlations of the EEG signals, it has been possible to detect relevant characteristics and differences in the brain’s activity. In conclusion, these findings are expected to help assess SM systems and give guidance to Industry 4.0 leaders.

result.paraphrase: The transition to Industry 4.0 can only be achieved by actively involving the shopfloor in the transformation process. Several shopfloor management (SM) systems can support this shift, and they fall into two main groups. The first comprises approaches such as the Balanced Scorecard (BSC), characterized by rigid structures focused on predefined goals. The other group of SM strategies emphasizes continuous improvement through guidance, with the “HOSHIN KANRI TREE” (HKT) as an example. One way to compare the differences, as well as the advantages and disadvantages, of these groups is to examine workers’ neurological patterns while they apply them. This paper seeks to do so using non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) sensors that record the brain’s electrical activity. A deep learning (DL) soft sensor classifies the recorded data with 96.5% accuracy. This result, together with an analysis of EEG signal correlations, made it possible to identify relevant characteristics and differences in brain activity. In conclusion, these findings are expected to support the evaluation of SM systems and provide guidance for Industry 4.0 leaders.
